record.paper_title: A Survey on Offline Reinforcement Learning: Taxonomy, Review, and Open Problems
record.original_question: How can offline reinforcement learning support a reliable end-to-end training workflow that selects hyperparameters, validates candidate policies during training, and decides when to stop training without any new interaction with the environment? In particular, the workflow must work from static logged data, avoid overfitting from repeatedly training on the same dataset, and replace the current practice of either depending on inaccurate off-policy evaluation or training for a fixed number of steps and evaluating the final policy online.

evidence.quote: One of the biggest open problems in offline RL is hyperparameter tuning [8]. Determining the set of hyperparameters that yield the best possible policy in an offline manner is extremely valuable, allowing us to save valuable resources and avoid dangerous interactions from online interaction. OPE is the task of evaluating a policy only through previous experiences. Excessively training on the same offline dataset can lead to poor solutions due to overfitting. Hence, it is paramount to find good OPE methods that allow us to validate our policy during training [65].

Currently, we either use inaccurate OPE methods for hyperparameter tuning or train for a fixed number of steps. These are both lackluster approaches since we are often left with a suboptimal policy that might have to overfit our data. Finding good ways to validate policies will also benefit training, allowing us to early stop training that exhibits degrading performance over time.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the offline reinforcement learning setting. A Markov decision process M = (S, A, P, r, γ, ρ₀) is given, but its transition kernel P and reward function r are unknown and cannot be queried. Instead, the learner is provided once and for all with a fixed logged dataset D = {(sᵢ, aᵢ, rᵢ, sᵢ')}ᵢ₌₁ᴺ generated by one or more unknown behavior policies, and may not collect any additional interaction with M during training, validation, hyperparameter tuning, or termination decisions.

Design an end-to-end training workflow A that takes as input D, a policy class Π_θ parameterized by θ, a learning algorithm parameterized by a finite set of hyperparameters H, and a computational budget, and outputs a single policy π̂ ∈ Π_θ, such that all of the following hold using only D (no environment access):

(i) Hyperparameter selection: A chooses a configuration h ∈ H whose resulting policy approximately maximizes the true expected return J(π) = E_{s₀∼ρ₀, aₜ∼π, sₜ₊₁∼P}[Σ_{t≥0} γᵗ r(sₜ, aₜ)].

(ii) Validation during training: At intermediate checkpoints {π^{(k)}}_k produced during optimization, A selects checkpoints with provably or empirically reliable estimates of J(π^{(k)}), avoiding the degradation caused by repeatedly training on the same dataset D.

(iii) Stopping rule: A determines a stopping time k* using only D-derived statistics such that J(π^{(k*)}) is close to max_k J(π^{(k)}), without relying on a pre-specified fixed number of gradient steps and without any online rollouts of the candidate policy.

(iv) Reliability guarantee: The workflow should come with quantitative guarantees (e.g., high-probability bounds, finite-sample regret with respect to the best in-class policy, or robustness certificates) that go beyond the use of standard off-policy evaluation estimators whose error is known to be large or whose own hyperparameters must themselves be tuned.

Provide such a workflow A together with assumptions on D, Π_θ, and M under which the above four properties simultaneously hold, or prove an impossibility result delineating regimes in which no such workflow can exist.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (2021–2025) actively studies subcomponents of this workflow: hyperparameter-free policy selection, offline policy selection sample complexity, and model selection for OPE. A 2023–2024 hardness result shows offline policy selection is in the worst case as hard as off-policy evaluation, and 2025 work continues to propose new selectors with theoretical guarantees, indicating that a fully reliable end-to-end offline workflow (selection + validation + stopping with guarantees) remains an open research problem.

status_evidence.title: When is Offline Hyperparameter Selection Feasible for Reinforcement Learning?
status_evidence.snippet: Holdout validation and hyperparameter tuning from data is a long-standing problem in offline RL... OPE either incurs exponential variance or has hyperparameters on their own.
status_evidence.claim: Offline hyperparameter selection remains a long-standing open problem with no fully reliable method.

status_evidence.title: Towards Hyperparameter-free Policy Selection for Offline RL
status_evidence.snippet: Existing approaches based on OPE often require additional function approximation and hence hyperparameters, creating a chicken-and-egg situation.
status_evidence.claim: Policy selection via OPE introduces its own hyperparameters, so the problem is not resolved.

status_evidence.title: When is Offline Policy Selection Sample Efficient for Reinforcement Learning?
status_evidence.snippet: A hardness result shows that in the worst case, OPS is just as hard as OPE.
status_evidence.claim: Worst-case hardness limits sample-efficient offline policy selection.

status_evidence.title: Model Selection for Off-policy Evaluation: New Algorithms and Experimental Protocol (2025)
status_evidence.snippet: Hyperparameter tuning for OPE itself is even more under-investigated... develops new selectors with theoretical guarantees.
status_evidence.claim: Active 2025 research continues to address OPE hyperparameter tuning, indicating the broader workflow remains open.
